name: Beta-glucan
short: Trials report mainly gastrointestinal symptoms, most frequent at the highest tablet dose; no major adverse events in a trial of an oat beta-glucan drink.
text: The main side effects reported in randomised trials were gastrointestinal. In a 4-week trial of an oat beta-glucan drink there were no major adverse events, but both the beta-glucan and the control drink transiently increased gastrointestinal symptoms. In a 12-week trial of beta-glucan tablets (1.5, 3 or 6 g daily), gastrointestinal adverse events were reported in 23.4%, 34.8% and 66.7% of the three beta-glucan groups and 36.9% of the placebo group. A 90-day trial of yeast-derived beta-glucan in adults aged 50 to 70 found it well tolerated. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.

quotes: There were no major adverse events, but both treatments transiently increased gastrointestinal symptoms.
